pageObservations.observations: Printed 1. Static Forces in Manipulators, Lecture 10 title, Pathak IIT Roorkee; campus image and institutional logos, no assessed technical proposition.
Printed 2. Objectives name velocity propagation, force and moment propagation, and evaluation and role of the Jacobian.
Printed 3. Outline lists velocity propagation, Jacobian, singularities, static forces, Jacobian force domain and Cartesian velocity/static-force transformations.

Printed 4. Two-link arm with coincident frame 0/1 origins and parallel frame 2/3 axes. T01 is Rz(theta1), T12 has x1 translation L1 and Rz(theta2), T23 is x2 translation L2. General modified-DH matrix wrongly prints row3col2 sin(alpha_i); direct Rx(alpha_(i-1))Rz(theta_i) gives sin(alpha_(i-1))cos(theta_i).
Printed 5. Fixed first origin v1=0, angular vector [0,0,q1dot]. Rotation R21 has first row [c2,s2,0] and leaves z unchanged. Adding q2dot z yields omega2=[0,0,q1dot+q2dot].

Printed 6. General first line labels output in frame i despite multiplication by R_(i+1,i). Worked frame2 calculation is consistent: cross product first gives [0,L1*q1dot,0], rotation gives [L1*s2*q1dot,L1*c2*q1dot,0].
Printed 7. Frames2/3 on same link; R32 identity. omega3 equals omega2, but v3 adds omega2 cross [L2,0,0], yielding [L1*s2*q1dot,L1*c2*q1dot+L2*(q1dot+q2dot),0].
Printed 8. Rotation R03=Rz(theta1+theta2) and explicit base velocity [-L1*s1*q1dot-L2*s12*(q1dot+q2dot), L1*c1*q1dot+L2*c12*(q1dot+q2dot),0].

Printed 9. Body Jacobian [[L1*s2,0],[L2+L1*c2,L2]] and base Jacobian [[-L1*s1-L2*s12,-L2*s12],[L1*c1+L2*c12,L2*c12]]. Slide equates a three-component vector with a two-row product, requiring explicit zero-z reduction.

Printed 10. Singularities described as lost Cartesian directions for joint-rate mapping. Determinant criterion shown in ongoing square 2R example; must not universalize determinant to a rectangular Jacobian or confuse instantaneous velocities with finite reachability.

Printed 11. Determinant L1*L2*sin(theta2), straight theta2=0 and folded theta2=180 degrees diagrams. With positive links each gives rank1 rather than zero generally, including equal folded lengths where second column remains [0,L2].

Printed 12. Inverse base Jacobian and unit +X command give q1dot=c12/(L1*s2), q2dot=-c1/(L2*s2)-c12/(L1*s2). Text claims both diverge approaching straight; this needs an incompatible-direction/path condition, since theta1=pi/2 gives finite exact (-1/L1,+1/L1). Figure elbow bend is labeled -theta2.

Printed13. Method locks joints into a structure, writes link force/moment balances, then computes static effort about each joint axis. Figure shows upstream and downstream forces/moments and vector P_(i+1) between origins.
Printed14. Gravity explicitly excluded. f_i and n_i are actions by link i-1 on link i. Thus link-i force balance f_i-f_(i+1)=0 uses opposite of the action on the next link.
Printed15. Moment balance n_i-n_(i+1)-P_(i+1) cross f_(i+1)=0. Known hand wrench propagates downward: f_i=R*nexf, n_i=R*nexn+P cross f_i, all additions in frame i.
Printed16. Revolute effort n dot z and prismatic effort f dot z; symbol tau used for both, so units differ. Positive torque tends to increase joint angle.
Printed17. Arm applies force in frame3. Frames2/3 aligned. No terminal couple in worked example; n2=L2*x2 cross [fx,fy,0]=[0,0,L2*fy]. fx lies along last link and gives no elbow moment.
Printed18. Force rotates by R12=Rz(theta2): [c2*fx-s2*fy,s2*fx+c2*fy,0]. n1z=L2*fy+L1*s2*fx+L1*c2*fy.
Printed19. tau1=L1*s2*fx+(L2+L1*c2)*fy, tau2=L2*fy. Matrix is transpose of earlier body Jacobian, not its inverse. All force components use same body frame as J3.

Printed20. Work is scalar energy; virtual work lets displacement become infinitesimal for statics. Need dot-product direction condition rather than claiming every motion under every force does nonzero work.

Printed21. Virtual work equates F^T*dchi=tau^T*dTheta; dchi=J*dTheta yields tau=J^T*F for arbitrary independent displacements. F and displacement6x1; joint vectors are labeled6x1 for six-joint case, not universal n. Work invariant under frame representation.

Printed22. Velocity order [v;omega], wrench [F;N]. Blue strike removes relative qdot term for fixed rigid-body frames. Linear recursion repeats frame-i output-label typo from p331. Final map X=[[R_BA,-R_BA*[p_AtoB]_cross],[0,R_BA]] with p expressed A.

Printed23. Wrench recursion and block map from B to A: [[R_AB,0],[[p_AtoB]_cross*R_AB,R_AB]], with p in A. Force only rotates; moment adds lever-arm cross rotated force. This is transpose of the opposite-direction velocity map.
Printed24. Summary states outward base-to-tip angular/linear propagation, v=J*qdot, singularity detJ=0 (square-case shorthand), tau=J^T*F. No extra terminal model beyond prior slides.

Printed25. Bibliography only: Craig2005 Introduction to Robotics Mechanics and Control3rd edition; Merzouki/Samantaray/Pathak/OuldBouamama2013 Intelligent Mechatronic Systems. No new assessable technical claim.
Printed26. Thank You only with footer logos; no assessable technical claim.

answers.reasoning: T01 has zero translation and Rz(theta1); T12 translates by [L1,0,0] in frame1 and rotates theta2; T23 translates [L2,0,0] with identity rotation.
Identity R23 implies parallel axes; its nonzero translation [L2,0,0] separates the origins.
Multiply row3 of Rx(alpha)=[0,sin(alpha),cos(alpha)] by column2 of Rz(theta)=[-sin(theta),cos(theta),0]; result sin(alpha)*cos(theta), with alpha_(i-1), not printed sin(alpha_i).
R21 is a z rotation, so R21*[0,0,q1dot]=[0,0,q1dot]; adding q2dot*z gives the sum.
The first joint origin is fixed while link1 rotates, so v1=0 and omega1=q1dot*z.
omega1 cross p12=[0,2,0]; R21 at30deg gives [2*sin30,2*cos30,0]=[1,sqrt(3),0] m/s.
R_(i+1,i) maps the frame-i bracket into frame i+1; therefore the left frame superscript must be i+1, as in the worked v2 equation.
Same rigid link and aligned axes share angular velocity; translating origin changes linear velocity by omega cross p23.
Compose R01*R12*R23=Rz(theta1+theta2), since R23=I.
Rz90 maps [x,y] to [-y,x], giving [-0.5,2,0] m/s.
Collect coefficients of q1dot and q2dot in v3: rows [L1*sin(theta2),0] and [L1*cos(theta2)+L2,L2].
Planar task retains x and y velocities; the identically zero z row is dropped, not combined with angular velocity.
Set q1dot=0,q2dot=1 in v3; second column is [0,L2] m/s.
Since v0=R03*v3 and v3=J3*qdot, left multiplication gives J0=R03*J3 for the same point and planar component basis.
Rank loss removes part of the instantaneous output-velocity range. It does not erase joint coordinates or exclude all later finite paths.
A determinant is a square-matrix criterion; rectangular Jacobians require the relevant rank condition.
With L1,L2>0, detJ=L1*L2*sin(theta2)=0 iff theta2=k*pi.
At theta1=theta2=0, base J=[[0,0],[L1+L2,L2]]; its range is the base Y axis.
With equal lengths and theta2=pi, body J=[[0,0],[L-L,L]]=[[0,0],[0,L]], rank1 because L>0.
At theta1=0,theta2=pi/2,L1=L2=1, J0=[[-1,-1],[1,0]]. Solving Jqdot=[1,0] gives q1dot=0, q2dot=-1 rad/s.
theta1=-theta2/2 gives c1=c12=cos(theta2/2); q1dot=cos(theta2/2)/sin(theta2)~1/theta2, q2dot=-2*cos(theta2/2)/sin(theta2)~-2/theta2. Signs are positive and negative approaching from above.
For theta1=pi/2, c1=0 and c12=-sin(theta2). Cancel nonzero sin(theta2): q1dot=-1/L1 and q2dot=+1/L1, finite; the source divergence statement is not universal.
Static method proceeds locked-joint structure, individual force/moment equilibrium, then projection on joint axis.
The slide explicitly omits link gravity, not terminal load or internal reactions.
f_(i+1) is the action by i on i+1. Newton third-law reaction on link i is -f_(i+1), producing the minus in its balance.
Given the terminal wrench boundary condition, recurse hand to base; forward velocity recursion is a different calculation.
The cross product is torque about origin i due to the force applied at offset p_(i+1).
A vector sum is meaningful only after both moments are expressed in frame i, so rotate downstream moment by R_(i,i+1).
For zero net force, p cross f=0. A free couple is unchanged by origin shift, although its coordinate components rotate.
Projection on unit joint axis uses dot products. Moment projection has N m units for revolute joints; force projection has N for prismatic joints.
n dot z=3*0-4*0+12*1=12 N m; norm13 is not the signed joint-axis component.
Positive actuator torque is the sense tending to increase the defined generalized joint angle, not a fixed world direction.
p23=L2*x2 and fx*x2 are parallel, so their cross product vanishes; fy gives L2*fy*z.
The two-link coefficient matrix is J3 transpose, so tau=J^T*F under the hand-applied load convention.
Power conjugacy requires common frames: F3=R30*F0, then tau=(J3)^T*F3. Joint effort indices are joints, not Cartesian directions.
theta2=0 makes sin(theta2)=0, and fy=0 eliminates all remaining terms, so both actuator torques vanish. Axial load still creates internal stresses and does not imply unlimited real capacity.
A pure z couple propagates without lever-arm additions and is unchanged by planar z rotations. Its projection adds M at both joints.
Virtual translational work is F dot dx=|F||dx|cos90=0.
Force dot displacement is scalar energy with units N*m=joules, distinct from a moment vector despite related dimensional units.
For independent joint coordinates the equality holds for every infinitesimal dq, forcing the coefficient vector J^T*F-tau to vanish. No invertibility is needed.
A spatial wrench has6 entries, J maps n joint rates to6 twist entries, and J^T*F gives n efforts: 6x1,6xn,nx1.
External environmental wrench has opposite sign to robot-on-environment load. Equilibrium is tau_act+J^T*F_ext=0, hence tau_act=-J^T*F_ext.
Source top block is translational velocity v and bottom angular omega; corresponding wrench top force F and bottom moment N.
Removing relative joint motion means frames attached to one rigid body, not that rotation matrices annihilate joint rates generally.
Velocity at B in A equals vA+omega cross p. Anticommutativity gives omega cross p=-p cross omega, so after rotation the upper-right block is -R[p]_cross.
omega cross p=[0,2,0]; vB in A=[1,2,0]; Rz(-90) maps [x,y] to [y,-x], giving [2,-1,0] m/s.
Force rotates from B to A. Moment about A equals rotated moment about B plus p_AtoB cross rotated force, using a common A basis.
Rz90*[2,0,0]=[0,2,0] N. Rotated couple remains [0,0,3]; p cross force=[0,0,2]; total [0,0,5] N m.
Substitute nuB=X*nuA into WB^T*nuB=(X^T*WB)^T*nuA. Equality for every nuA gives WA=X^T*WB.
With p=0 the cross-product offset blocks vanish; both types of vector map by separate rotation blocks, with direction-appropriate rotations.
Joint-rate boundary data propagate velocities outward base to tip. Terminal force/moment boundary data propagate static loads inward tip to base.
